ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A 3-phase, 440 V, 50 Hz, 4-pole slip ring induction motor is fed from the rotor side through an auto-transformer, and the stator is connected to a variable resistance as shown in the figure.

The motor is coupled to a 220 V, separately excited D.C. generator feeding power to a fixed resistance of 10 \( \Omega \). Two-wattmeter method is used to measure the input power to the induction motor. The variable resistance is adjusted such that the motor runs at 1410 rpm, and the following readings were recorded:

\( W_1 = 1800 W \), \( W_2 = -200 W \).

The speed of rotation of the stator magnetic field with respect to the rotor structure will be:
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: 1500 rpm in the opposite direction of rotation

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is labeled “3-phase, 50 Hz, Supply”, connected through “Auto Transformer” to the left-side terminals of the induction motor; above the motor is connected a three-phase variable resistor; the motor shaft is coupled to the right to a DC generator, the generator output terminals are connected to a load resistor, and a 220 V excitation power supply is also drawn beside it. Therefore the illustrated structure is consistent with the problem meaning: the rotor side is supplied by a three-phase 50 Hz power supply through an autotransformer, the stator side is connected to a variable resistor, and on the shaft there is a separately excited DC generator and load. Reasoning: The rotor is supplied by a 50 Hz three-phase power supply, so relative to the rotor structure, the synchronous speed of the rotating magnetic field produced by this power supply is Ns = 120f/P = 120 × 50 / 4 = 1500 rpm. The direction still needs to be determined. The total input power from the two wattmeter readings is W1 + W2 = 1800 + (-200) = 1600 W, which is positive, indicating that electrical power is input to the induction motor; the right-side DC generator and 10 Ω resistor constitute the mechanical load. If the magnetic field produced by rotor supply rotates in the same direction relative to the rotor, then its speed relative to stationary space is about 1410 + 1500 = 2910 rpm, which is inconsistent with the power/torque direction under the condition of this passive stator resistor and generator load. If the magnetic field rotates in the reverse direction relative to the rotor, then its space speed is 1410 - 1500 = -90 rpm, which is consistent with the situation in which the motor absorbs electrical power and drives the DC generator load. Therefore the magnitude of the speed of this magnetic field relative to the rotor structure is 1500 rpm, and the direction is opposite to the mechanical rotation direction of the rotor.

method.method_draft: First describe the image connections: rotor fed from the 3-phase supply through the auto-transformer, stator loaded by variable resistance, and shaft coupled to a DC generator/load. From the text, compute the speed of the rotating field produced by the 50 Hz rotor supply relative to the rotor structure: Ns = 120*50/4 = 1500 rpm. The field could be in either direction depending on rotor phase sequence. Use W1 + W2 = 1800 - 200 = 1600 W, so electrical power is being supplied to the induction motor, and the pictured DC generator/resistor is a mechanical load. Test the two possible reference-frame sums: if the rotor-supply field were in the same direction as rotor rotation, its space speed would be 1410 + 1500 = 2910 rpm, which gives the wrong power/torque sense for this passive-stator, generator-loaded motor. If it is opposite to rotor rotation, the space speed is 1410 - 1500 = -90 rpm, consistent with motoring while delivering shaft power and dissipating stator induced power. Therefore the stator magnetic field, locked to the air-gap field, rotates at 1500 rpm with respect to the rotor structure, opposite to rotor rotation.

method.method_draft: First state what the image shows: rotor excitation from the 3-phase supply through the auto-transformer, passive stator resistor load, and a shaft-coupled DC generator load. Since the rotor winding is the supplied 3-phase winding, the magnetic field associated with the stator/air-gap reaction must rotate synchronously relative to the rotor at Ns = 120*50/4 = 1500 rpm. The only remaining issue is direction. The text and image show a motor driving a generator load, so the electromagnetic torque must be in the same direction as the rotor's mechanical rotation. With a passive stator resistance, Lenz-law reaction gives motoring torque only when the air-gap field is produced by a rotor phase sequence that is opposite to the rotor's mechanical rotation; then the field is nearly stationary in space with speed 1410 - 1500 = -90 rpm, a plausible small slip-field speed. A same-direction rotor field would sweep past the stator at 1410 + 1500 rpm and correspond to the wrong braking/generating sense. Hence, relative to the rotor structure, the stator magnetic field speed is 1500 rpm and its direction is opposite to the rotor rotation.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that a balanced 3-phase winding supplied at frequency f produces an MMF rotating at 120f/P relative to that winding. Use Lenz-law/induction-machine torque direction: currents in a passive stator resistance oppose the relative motion of the air-gap flux, so for the rotor to develop motoring torque while running at 1410 rpm, the rotor-produced field must be counter-rotating relative to the rotor rather than forward-rotating.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是标注为3-phase, 50 Hz Supply的电源，经Auto Transformer接到感应电机的滑环/转子侧；电机上方接有三相可变电阻；电机轴向右机械耦合到一台直流发电机，发电机接负载电阻并有220 V独立励磁。推理：因为三相50 Hz电源加在4极转子绕组上，三相转子电流产生的旋转磁场相对于转子结构的同步转速为 Ns = 120f/P = 120×50/4 = 1500 rpm。图中电机带动直流发电机和电阻负载，且两瓦特表总输入 W1 + W2 = 1600 W 为正，所以它处于电动运行，电磁转矩应与转子机械转向一致。定子侧只是无源电阻负载；为产生电动转矩，转子相序应使气隙/定子反应磁场相对于转子朝机械转向的相反方向转动。这样该场在空间中的速度为 1410 - 1500 = -90 rpm，符合小滑差运行；若同向则相对定子扫过约 2910 rpm，趋势不符合该电动运行状态。因此相对于转子结构，定子磁场速度为1500 rpm，方向与转子旋转方向相反。
solver_metadata.model_answer: 1500 rpm, in the opposite direction to the rotor's mechanical rotation.

raw_record.original_question:
A 3-phase, 440 V, 50 Hz, 4-pole slip ring induction motor is fed from the rotor side through an auto-transformer, and the stator is connected to a variable resistance as shown in the figure.

The motor is coupled to a 220 V, separately excited D.C. generator feeding power to a fixed resistance of 10 \( \Omega \). Two-wattmeter method is used to measure the input power to the induction motor. The variable resistance is adjusted such that the motor runs at 1410 rpm, and the following readings were recorded:

\( W_1 = 1800\,W \), \( W_2 = -200\,W \).

What is the speed of rotation of the stator magnetic field with respect to the rotor structure, and in which direction does it rotate?
raw_record.answer: 1500 rpm in the opposite direction of rotation
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The left side of the figure is labeled “3-phase, 50 Hz, Supply”, connected through “Auto Transformer” to the left-side terminals of the induction motor; above the motor is connected a three-phase variable resistor; the motor shaft is coupled to the right to a DC generator, the generator output terminals are connected to a load resistor, and a 220 V excitation power supply is also drawn beside it. Therefore the illustrated structure is consistent with the problem meaning: the rotor side is supplied by a three-phase 50 Hz power supply through an autotransformer, the stator side is connected to a variable resistor, and on the shaft there is a separately excited DC generator and load.

Reasoning: The rotor is supplied by a 50 Hz three-phase power supply, so relative to the rotor structure, the synchronous speed of the rotating magnetic field produced by this power supply is Ns = 120f/P = 120 × 50 / 4 = 1500 rpm. The direction still needs to be determined. The total input power from the two wattmeter readings is W1 + W2 = 1800 + (-200) = 1600 W, which is positive, indicating that electrical power is input to the induction motor; the right-side DC generator and 10 Ω resistor constitute the mechanical load. If the magnetic field produced by rotor supply rotates in the same direction relative to the rotor, then its speed relative to stationary space is about 1410 + 1500 = 2910 rpm, which is inconsistent with the power/torque direction under the condition of this passive stator resistor and generator load. If the magnetic field rotates in the reverse direction relative to the rotor, then its space speed is 1410 - 1500 = -90 rpm, which is consistent with the situation in which the motor absorbs electrical power and drives the DC generator load. Therefore the magnitude of the speed of this magnetic field relative to the rotor structure is 1500 rpm, and the direction is opposite to the mechanical rotation direction of the rotor.
